description.zh: 物体离凸透镜远近不同，像的大小、正倒、虚实都会变：物距大于二倍焦距成缩小倒立的实像，在一倍与二倍焦距之间成放大倒立的实像，小于一倍焦距成放大正立的虚像——三条特殊光线就能画出像在哪里。
description.en: How far an object sits from a convex lens changes the image’s size, orientation and kind: beyond twice the focal length it is a smaller inverted real image, between one and two focal lengths a larger inverted real image, and inside one focal length a larger upright virtual image — three special rays locate it.

zh: 一倍焦距分虚实，二倍焦距分大小
en: f splits real from virtual, 2f splits larger from smaller

reason.zh: 光进出透镜两个表面各折射一次；凸透镜中间厚、边缘薄，越靠边的光偏折越多，平行光就被收拢到焦点。
reason.en: Light refracts once entering and once leaving the lens; a convex lens is thicker in the middle than at the edge, so rays nearer the rim bend more and parallel light converges at the focus.

reason.zh: 小孔只靠光沿直线传播就成倒像，放大率是 −v/u；透镜把更多的光会聚到同一个像点，像更亮，同一个 M = −v/u 仍给出像的大小和正倒。
reason.en: A pinhole forms an inverted image from straight-line light alone, with magnification −v/u; a lens gathers far more light into each image point for a brighter image, and the same M = −v/u still gives its size and orientation.

label.zh: 眼睛是一枚可调的凸透镜
label.en: The eye is an adjustable convex lens

reason.zh: 眼睛把晶状体当凸透镜、视网膜当光屏，成倒立缩小的实像；看远看近要调节焦距，像落不到视网膜上就是近视或远视。
reason.en: The eye uses its lens as a convex lens and the retina as the screen, forming a smaller inverted real image; it adjusts its focal length for near and far, and an image that misses the retina is short- or long-sightedness.

question.zh: 放大镜为什么能把字放大？
question.en: Why does a magnifying glass make text look bigger?

ask.zh: 把字放在一倍焦距以内，像是实像还是虚像、正立还是倒立？
ask.en: With the text inside one focal length, is the image real or virtual, upright or inverted?

ask.zh: 光穿过凸透镜为什么会往中间偏？
ask.en: Why does light bend toward the middle as it passes through a convex lens?

reveal.zh: 字在一倍焦距以内时，折射后的光不再相交，眼睛顺着它们的反向延长线看到一个正立、放大的虚像。屏接不住这个像，只能透过透镜去看。
reveal.en: With the text inside one focal length, the refracted rays no longer meet; the eye traces them back and sees an upright, magnified virtual image. No screen can catch it — you can only look through the lens.
